ei)s or e)s, PREP. WITH ACC. ONLY:—both forms are found in Hom. , Ion. poets, and early metrical Inscrr.; e)s is best attested in Hdt. and Hp. , and is found in nearly all early Ion. Inscrr. (exc. IG 12(8).262.16 (Thasos, v B. C.), ib. 7.235.1 (Oropus, iv B. C.)); ei)s in Att. Inscrr. from iv B. C., IG 2.115 , etc.; and usu. in Att. Prose (exc. Th. ) and Com. (exc. in parody): Trag. apptly. prefer ei)s, but e)s is used before vowels metri gr.; e)s was retained in the phrases e)s ko/rakas (whence the Verb skoraki/zw), e)s makari/an. Aeol. poets have ei)s before vowels, e)s before consonants, and this is given as the rule in Hom. by An.Ox. 1.172 , cf. Hellad. ap. Phot. Bibl. p.533B. (Orig. e)ns, as in IG 4.554.7 (Argos), GDI 4986.11 (Crete); cf. e)n, i)n. The diphthong is genuine in Aeol.
